items.title: Herb Morand Interview, 1950-03-12
items.q: It caused the band to split up in Bristol, Oklahoma. We split up. Frank Pasley, he went to Chicago.

ctx.x: That was a sub year, around 1923. So, after we left Devonport, we started booking dances. After our contract was up, we started booking dances, playing theaters all over the state of Oklahoma. We got a booking agent, and we played such theaters like the Rialto in Tulsa. The first real theater I ever played in, and they gave us a nice write-up. It was crazy about the jazz band. items.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23
items.q: They had one trombone player named Lewis and Herbert Mourney.

ctx.x: I was born in 1904 in New Orleans, Louisiana. Which day? November 11th. Oh, yeah. And I played with the old, the old, the old Olympia band with Arnold De Pass. He's a drummer. He had a band around there. Oh, I think he played with Kid Punch too. Yeah. Well, they were much older musicians than me.
Excuse me. Who else was with you and Arnold De Pass in that band? Well, I can't call what.

They had one trombone player named Lewis and Herbert Mourney. Herbert Mouran. Herbert Mouran. Yeah, Herbert Mouran. Yeah. The Harlem band. Yeah. Let's see who else. I had a little fellow named Lewis played a clan that had been so long ago. I can't call all those. Not Josh Lewis? No. I never did play with George Lewis. Oh, yeah. I had left. See, I left New Orleans in 1924.
